question.text: Is patient outcome compromised during the initial experience with robot-assisted radical cystectomy?
question.context: • Robot-assisted radical cystectomy (RARC) remains controversial in terms of oncologic outcomes, especially during the initial experience. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the impact of initial experience of robotic cystectomy programs on oncologic outcomes and overall survival. • Utilizing a prospectively maintained, single institution robotic cystectomy database, we identified 164 consecutive patients who underwent RARC since November 2005. • After stratification by age group, gender, pathologic T stage, lymph node status, surgical margin status, and sequential case number; we used chi-squared analyses to correlate sequential case number to operative time, surgical blood loss, lymph node yield, and surgical margin status. • We also addressed the relationship between complications and sequential case number. We then utilized Cox proportional hazard modeling and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses to correlate variables to overall mortality. • Sequential case number was not significantly associated with increased incidence of complications, surgical blood loss, or positive surgical margins (P= 0.780, P= 0.548, P= 0.545). Case number was, however, significantly associated with shorter operative time and mean number of lymph nodes retrieved (P<0.001, P<0.001). • Sequential case number was not significantly associated with survival; however, tumour stage, the presence of lymph node metastases, and positive surgical margins were significantly associated with death. • Although being the largest of its kind, this was a small study with short follow-up when compared to open cystectomy series.

medgemma_4b.clinical_reasoning: The study found no significant association between sequential case number and overall mortality, complications, surgical blood loss, or positive surgical margins. While the study has limitations (small sample size and short follow-up), the lack of association between case number and survival suggests that initial experience with RARC does not compromise patient outcomes.
medgemma_4b.critical_evidence: Sequential case number was not significantly associated with survival.
medgemma_4b.differential_considered: While the study has limitations, the lack of association between case number and survival suggests that initial experience with RARC does not compromise patient outcomes. The study's limitations should be considered when interpreting the results.

rnj1_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study found that patient outcomes were not compromised during the initial experience with robot-assisted radical cystectomy. Sequential case number was not significantly associated with complications, surgical blood loss, or positive surgical margins. While operative time and lymph node yield decreased with experience, these factors did not indicate compromised outcomes. The study concluded that oncologic outcomes and overall survival were not significantly affected by the level of experience with robotic cystectomy.
rnj1_8b.critical_evidence: Sequential case number was not significantly associated with increased incidence of complications, surgical blood loss, or positive surgical margins (P= 0.780, P= 0.548, P= 0.545)
rnj1_8b.differential_considered: The study specifically addressed the question of compromised outcomes during initial robotic cystectomy experience, and the data directly supports that outcomes were not compromised. No other factors were found to be significantly associated with patient outcomes in this analysis.

qwen3_vl_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study found that sequential case number was not significantly associated with complications, blood loss, positive margins, or survival outcomes. Although operative time and lymph node yield improved with experience, these did not translate to compromised patient outcomes. The key oncologic predictors of mortality were tumor stage, lymph node metastases, and positive margins—not the surgeon’s initial experience.
qwen3_vl_8b.critical_evidence: Sequential case number was not significantly associated with survival; however, tumour stage, the presence of lymph node metastases, and positive surgical margins were significantly associated with death.
qwen3_vl_8b.differential_considered: Considered whether initial robotic experience might compromise outcomes, but ruled it out because the study showed no significant association between case number and complications, margins, or survival—only technical efficiency improved with experience.

olmo3_7b.critical_evidence: Case number was not significantly associated with complications or overall survival, and was not significantly associated with positive surgical margins or increased blood loss.
